notes: LUM-1332 — the *before* half of the A/B: the pre-fix binary over the same gestures as lum1332-composer-drag-select.json.

Every panel asserts the defect positively — no '# reverse' run anywhere (nothing was selected) and no '# clipboard' write (nothing was copied) — so this file is evidence of the gap, not a passing gate. Run it against the binary built from the parent commit:

Panel 3 is the exception and it is deliberate: the plain *click* is LUM-1327's, already fixed in the parent commit, so this file pins that the click still places the caret while every drag next to it does nothing.
Geometry is the post-fix file's: composer rows 17-18, status bar 19, label gutter columns 0-1.
Panels 1, 2, 3 (and 4/5, 6/7) share a grid on purpose: the defect *is* 'the frame does not change', so the harness' duplicate-frame warnings are the finding here, not a defect of the scenario.
caption: LUM-1332 — the same pointer gestures against the pre-fix binary (100x20, real PTY). Panels 1-2: dragging across 'llo wo' highlights nothing, moves nothing and copies nothing — the composer consumed the drag and the release and threw both away, leaving only the caret LUM-1327's press placed on the pressed character. Panel 3: the same cell clicked — the click (LUM-1327) is what places the caret, so this panel is byte-identical to panels 1-2 on purpose. Panels 4-5: a drag across a line break likewise selects nothing and copies nothing. Panels 6-7: a drag that leaves the composer selects nothing, and its release copies nothing. The '# reverse' / '# clipboard' evidence lines the harness would print for a selection are absent from every panel. This is the state lum1332-composer-drag-select.json fixes.

and it did not follow the drag to the end either

the release of a drag that never selected has nothing to copy
one caret, exactly where the press left it

the caret is where the press put it
